name: Mute Records
ownershipStory: Daniel Miller founded Mute in 1978 to release his own synthesizer single as the Normal, 'T.V.O.D.' backed with 'Warm Leatherette', which sold well enough through Rough Trade to keep the label going. He signed Depeche Mode on a verbal agreement after seeing them in Canning Town in 1980, and their worldwide success paid for Mute's growth. EMI bought the label for £23 million in 2002 with Miller still running it; in 2010 he set up a new independent Mute Artists company while the Mute Records catalogue stayed with EMI's successors.
hook: A one-man synthesizer label that signed Depeche Mode on a handshake and grew with them.

blurb.age13: Daniel Miller started Mute Records in London in 1978 to put out his own electronic single. In 1980 he saw a young synth band from Basildon, Depeche Mode, and signed them with a spoken agreement instead of a written contract. They became huge, and so did Mute.
blurb.adult: Mute is the independent-label counterpart to Factory on this map: artist-friendly, electronic from the start, and carried by one act's success. The 2002 EMI sale and the 2010 split between the old catalogue company and a new independent one show how the ownership of an 'independent' label's history can end up with a major.
